### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

Attempting to use the `include` parameter to `model_dump` when the model has a `@model_serializer` method causes a `PydanticOmit` exception to be returned.

### Example Code

```Python
from pydantic import BaseModel, model_serializer

class Foo(BaseModel):
    bar:int
    baz:int

    @model_serializer(mode='wrap')
    def _serialize(self, next_serializer, info):
        return next_serializer(self, info)

f = Foo(bar=123, baz=456)

print(f.model_dump(include={'bar'}))
```

Output:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/phemmer/.config/JetBrains/PyCharm2025.1/scratches/scratch_12.py", line 9, in _serialize
    return next_serializer(self, info)
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.PydanticOmit: PydanticOmit()

The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/phemmer/.config/JetBrains/PyCharm2025.1/scratches/scratch_12.py", line 13, in <module>
    print(f.model_dump(include={'bar'}))
          ~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/home/phemmer/.local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/pydantic/main.py", line 463, in model_dump
    return self.__pydantic_serializer__.to_python(
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^
        self,
        ^^^^^
    ...<11 lines>...
        serialize_as_any=serialize_as_any,
        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    )
    ^
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.PydanticSerializationError: Error calling function `_serialize`: PydanticOmit: PydanticOmit()
```
